title: Add a device
finding: Sends Wi-Fi, this server’s address and the time zone over Bluetooth. Your browser talks to the device; the server never sees the Wi-Fi password, and no PetKit app is involved.
browserNote: Web Bluetooth needs Chrome or Edge on desktop or Android, and a secure context: a page with a trusted certificate. On an iPhone, use the MyPetKit app.

status.provisioned: Provisioned. The device will restart and join Wi-Fi.
status.unanswered: Sent, but the device never answered.
status.connected: Device connected. See the Devices page.
status.missingWifi: The Wi-Fi name and password are both required.

found.empty: No device chosen yet. Use Find device, then pick it from the browser’s list.

environment.insecureTooltip: Web Bluetooth needs a secure page, and this one is plain HTTP. See the note above.
environment.noBluetoothTooltip: This browser has no Web Bluetooth. Use Chrome or Edge, on desktop or Android.
environment.insecure: Web Bluetooth only works on a secure page, and this one is plain HTTP. Serve Home Assistant over HTTPS with your own certificate; provisioning then works from this page, Ingress included. You will need Chrome or Edge as well. A plain-HTTP page cannot tell whether you have one, because the browser hides Web Bluetooth entirely until the page is secure. Or use the hosted provisioning page at <hosted>{{url}}</hosted>, which runs entirely in your browser and talks to the device over Bluetooth. It never sees your Wi-Fi password.
environment.noBluetooth: This browser has no Web Bluetooth. It is only in Chrome and Edge, on desktop or Android; Firefox, Safari and iOS cannot provision. On an iPhone, use the MyPetKit app.

form.wifiNameHint: The network the device will join, not necessarily the one this browser is on.
form.passwordHint: Required: an open network cannot be provisioned this way. It goes from this page to the device over Bluetooth, never to this server or to PetKit.
form.serverUrlHint: Burned in at provisioning: use an IP, or a name the device itself can resolve.
form.serverFailed: Could not read this server’s address ({{error}}). Type it in, or retry.
form.timeZoneHint: The device has no clock settings of its own: it keeps this fixed offset, with no daylight saving. Changing it later means provisioning again.
form.note: The address comes from your server, not from this browser. Hold the device’s button until it beeps, then choose it from the browser’s list.

warning.mdnsHost: This address uses a .local mDNS host, which most PetKit devices cannot resolve. Use the server’s IP instead, for example http://<server-ip>/6/.
warning.notPort80: ESP32 devices such as T4 and D4 need the server on port 80. Provisioning them will fail with this address.
